name: Twill
author: E. T. Carter
description: A twill weave, the diagonal cloth of denim and gabardine. Warp threads float over two wefts then duck under one, the float shifting a thread each row so the raised segments stack into bright diagonal wales running across the cloth. A combed sheen travels along the diagonal so the ribs catch the light in sequence, threads tinted by their diagonal band. A woven-flow sibling of warp-current — combed into ruled twill rather than free domain-warped fibre.

params.label: Thread spacing
params.effect: Distance between threads in CSS px; a fine tight twill at the minimum, a coarse open weave at the maximum.

params.label: Thread width
params.effect: Half-width of each thread in CSS px with its halo; fine yarn to thick glowing cord.

params.label: Wale steepness
params.effect: How far the float shifts each row; 0 gives vertical floats (no diagonal), high steepens the wales into a sharp diagonal twill.

params.label: Sheen
params.effect: Strength of the diagonal light sweep along the wales; 0 is a matte twill, high a bright denim glint.

params.label: Sheen speed
params.effect: Speed the sheen runs along the diagonal ribs; 0 holds it still, high sweeps it briskly.

params.label: Glow
params.effect: Overall thread emission; low is a quiet cloth, high a luminous woven sheet.

params.label: Relief
params.effect: How strongly the raised floats outshine the threads passing under; 0 flattens to a plain grid, high makes the diagonal wales stand out as raised ribs.
